From: Elena Ruiz <elena@atlashealth.com>

Cc: procurement@atlashealth.com, m.donovan@atlashealth.com
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Clarify termination & auto-renew language on Order Form

Hi Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Atlas is excited about Redwood. Procurement asked me to flag two items on the Order Form draft we received: the auto-renew clause and the "termination for convenience" language. They want to understand

- whether auto-renew is unconditional at the end of each term or whether we can add a 60-day notice requirement to prevent a surprise renewal, and
- what the practical support/transition commitments look like if we exercise termination for convenience (items like data export assistance, retained snapshots, and any pro-rated credits).

Can you point to the specific MSA/Order Form paragraphs we should be looking at and confirm whether Redwood is open to a 60-day mutual notice for auto-renew and a short handback SLA for TFC?

We'd like to keep momentum on the purchase order this month, so a quick response would be appreciated.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz\Director of Procurement\Atlas Health

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. Looping in Karthik and Ben to propose a customer-friendly path. Short answers up front: yes, we're generally open to a mutual 60-day notice window at renewal; and we can put a targeted handback commitment into the Order Form for termination-for-convenience with a defined set of deliverables.

Karthik/Ben — can you share preferred wording and any pricing considerations if Atlas wants a 60-day mutual notice (versus our standard 30-day auto-renew)? If legal prefers a different framing for the TFC handback, please propose redline text.

I'll coordinate the updated Order Form once we have language.

Best,
Laura Bennett\Account Executive, Enterprise Sales\Redwood Inference\laura_bennett@redwood.com\(415) 555-0134

Subject: Re: Clarify termination & auto-renew language on Order Form

Thanks Laura / Elena —

Agreeing with Laura's leaning. Proposed commercial compromise:

- Auto-renew: mutual 60-day notice for both parties. If Atlas provides notice within the 60-day window, the renewal is cancelled. Outside that window, the term auto-renews for the same length. If Atlas asks for the 60-day window as a non-negotiable, we may need a modest one-time setup credit to compensate timing risk; happy to discuss.

- Termination for Convenience: Redwood will commit to a 30-day targeted handback assistance period, including: export of customer-owned data in standard formats, an operational playbook for service transfer, and up to 8 hours of technical migration support. We will provide pro-rata refunds for pre-paid unused months where applicable.

I've attached a redline to the Order Form highlighting the suggested edits and a separate matrix that maps notice windows to pricing/credits. If this looks OK to Atlas, Laura and I can get Legal to prepare final redline for the MSA.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer\Senior Director, Sales\Redwood Inference\karthik_iyer@redwood.com

From: ben_carter@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Clarify termination & auto-renew language on Order Form

Laura / Karthik / Elena —

Industrializing a few legal points so procurement can route to counsel easily: below is redline-ready language we prefer and rationale. I'm including it here so Atlas procurement has full context before formal MSA edits.

1) Auto-Renew (Order Form, Section 2.1) — Proposed: "This Order Form will automatically renew for successive term(s) equal to the Initial Term unless either party provides written notice of non-renewal at least sixty (60) days prior to the then-current term end date." Rationale: mutual 60-day notice is balanced; avoids asymmetry.

2) Termination for Convenience (MSA, Section 9.2) — Proposed summary clause for Order Form: "Customer may terminate this Order Form for convenience upon sixty (60) days' prior written notice. Upon such termination, Redwood will provide a thirty (30) day handback assistance period at no additional charge, which will include (i) export of Customer data in commonly used formats, (ii) delivery of an operations playbook and configuration snapshots, and (iii) up to eight (8) hours of technical support to assist with transfer. Any pre-paid fees for Services not delivered as of the effective termination date will be refunded on a pro-rata basis within thirty (30) days." Rationale: tight, prescriptive deliverables reduce future disputes.

3) Exceptions & Escrow — If Atlas requires an extended handback (beyond 30 days) or a guaranteed SLA for large-scale migrations, we would treat that as a billable Professional Services add-on and include an addendum.

Action: If Atlas signs off on the above, I'll convert to tracked-changes against the MSA + Order Form and circulate a single redline doc for signature.

Ben Carter\Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts\Redwood Inference\ben_carter@redwood.com

If you can circulate the tracked-changes redline today, Procurement will route to our legal and we should be positioned to sign early next week. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
